mainTopic: מעילה after an item's מצוה is done, the wine of the נסכים in the pipes, and items that are forbidden but carry no מעילה
overview: The גמרא is working with the rule that once an item's מצוה is done, מעילה no longer applies to it. It challenges this rule with תרומת הדשן, which still carries מעילה after its מצוה. The answer is that two cases sharing an unusual law (שני כתובין הבאין כאחד) do not teach a general rule. The גמרא pairs תרומת הדשן first with the scapegoat's limbs, then with the בגדי כהונה, then with עגלה ערופה, so the answer works for each opinion. For the view that two such cases do teach, it points to an exclusion word in each פסוק. Next, the גמרא asks whether the משנה about נסכים fits רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק, who says the hardened wine in the pipes is burned בקדושה. Two versions are given, and in the second, the burning is only מדרבנן and the פסוק is an אסמכתא. Finally, a new משנה lists items that may not be used but carry no מעילה, and the גמרא begins its question on it, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from the removal of the ashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that there is no מעילה after an item's מצוה is done, pointing to תרומת הדשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at תרומת הדשן: its מצוה has already been done, and it is still subject to מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule that an item is free of מעילה once its מצוה is done. It brings תרומת הדשן as a case that seems to prove the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes are lifted off the מזבח and placed beside it, which completes their מצוה. Yet they still carry מעילה. So the case seems to show that finishing the מצוה does not end מעילה, and that could undo the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily removal of a portion of ashes from the מזבח, which are then placed beside it
Its מצוה has been done, meaning the item has fulfilled its holy purpose
The prohibition against using or benefiting from הקדש (holy property)

phrases.english: But there is the removal of the ashes,
whose מצוה has been performed,
and it is still subject to misuse of consecrated property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from the earlier part of the daf that there is no מעילה after an item's מצוה is done.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that once an item's מצוה is done, it no longer carries מעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-example: תרומת הדשן has finished its מצוה and still carries מעילה, so the opposite rule could be learned from it.

steps.title: Two special cases do not teach a general rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תרומת הדשן and the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח are שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, so they teach nothing for other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule. It says תרומת הדשן is one of two exceptions, and two exceptions cannot be used to build a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה had to state the same unusual law in two separate places, that shows the law is limited to those cases. Otherwise one mention would have been enough to teach everything. So תרומת הדשן stays an exception, and the general rule of no מעילה after the מצוה survives.

keyTerms.meaning: The limbs of the scapegoat sent off on יום כפור after it was pushed off the cliff
Two verses that come as one: two cases in the תורה that share the same unusual law
They do not teach, meaning the law cannot be applied to other cases

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this answer says תרומת הדשן lacks מעילה. It clearly has מעילה. The answer only says this case is an exception that cannot be stretched to other items.

phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes
and the limbs of the scapegoat
are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְאֵיבְרֵי שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from תרומת הדשן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the counter-example by showing it is one of two exceptions that do not teach a general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומת הדשן proves that items still carry מעילה after their מצוה is done.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומת הדשן and the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח are שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, so nothing is learned from them for other cases.

steps.title: What about the view that the scapegoat's limbs are permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the answer only works for the view that the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח are forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says we may not benefit from the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח. But for the one who says we may benefit from them, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the previous answer. According to one opinion, the scapegoat's limbs are permitted, so they cannot be the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer needed two cases that carry מעילה after their מצוה. If the scapegoat's limbs may be used, only תרומת הדשן is left. With only one case, the rule of שני כתובין no longer applies, and the original challenge comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well. It accepts an answer for one view in order to challenge it for another view
One may benefit from them
What is there to say? Asks for an answer that works for the other view

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who said

phrases.aramaic: אֵיבְרֵי שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ – אֵין נֶהֱנִין מֵהֶן,
phrases.english: that one may not derive benefit from the limbs of the scapegoat,
but according to the one who said one may derive benefit from them,
what can be said?!
phrases.notes: He means: by that view תרומת הדשן stands alone, so why can't we learn from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 2 based on a disagreement about the scapegoat's limbs.
steps.kashyaTarget: The pairing of תרומת הדשן with the limbs of the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the view that the limbs are permitted, they lack מעילה, so there is no second case and the rule of שני כתובין cannot be used.

steps.title: A different partner: the priestly garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תרומת הדשן pairs with the בגדי כהונה instead, so they are still שני כתובין הבאין כאחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and the בגדי כהונה are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rescues its answer by finding a different second case: the white garments of the כהן גדול from יום כפור, which also carry מעילה after their מצוה is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic stays the same, and only the partner case changes. The בגדי כהונה also stay forbidden after their מצוה is done, so there are still two exceptions and nothing can be learned from them. The next step shows that even this pairing depends on a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly garments, here meaning the white garments of the כהן גדול worn on יום כפור
Because it is. Introduces the reason for the answer
And any. Signals that a general rule is being stated

steps.whatToRemember: Two cases that share an unusual law (שני כתובין הבאין כאחד) do not teach that law for other cases. That is why תרומת הדשן, paired either with the scapegoat's limbs or with the בגדי כהונה, does not overturn the rule that there is no מעילה after an item's מצוה is done.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: when one partner case is disputed, the גמרא swaps in another partner so that the answer also works for the opinion that rejected the first one.

phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes
and the priestly vestments
phrases.notes: These are the white garments of the כהן גדול on יום כפור, which the פסוק says must be left there (ויקרא 16:23).

phrases.english: are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וּבִגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 3 by replacing the scapegoat's limbs with the בגדי כהונה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Swaps the partner case so the principle of שני כתובין works according to all views.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to the view that permits the scapegoat's limbs, תרומת הדשן stands alone and should teach a general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומת הדשן pairs with the בגדי כהונה as שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, so it still teaches nothing for other cases.

steps.title: The garments pairing fails for רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The pairing of תרומת הדשן with the כהן גדול's יום הכיפורים garments works for the רבנן, who require גניזה. It fails for רבי דוסא, who lets an ordinary כהן use them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the רבנן, who learn from 'and he shall leave them there' that the garments must be hidden away. But according to רבי דוסא, who says an ordinary כהן may use them, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 4. That answer depends on the garments being forbidden after use, and רבי דוסא disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the garments must be put away (גניזה) after the עבודה, so they stay forbidden even after their מצוה is done, just like תרומת הדשן. That makes two sources, and two sources that say the same thing do not teach a general rule. For רבי דוסא the garments may be used afterward, so תרומת הדשן stands alone again, and a lone source should teach a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one opinion, but…)
Putting a holy item away so no one uses it
An ordinary כהן (not the כהן גדול)
What is there to say? (a challenge asking for an answer)

steps.confusionAlert: The garments here are the white garments the כהן גדול wore on יום הכיפורים. They are not all בגדי כהונה in general.

phrases.english: This works well according to the Rabbis, who say:
"And he shall leave them there"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:23, about the white garments of the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: teaches that they need to be hidden away, so it works fine.
But according to Rabbi Dosa, who said:
an ordinary priest is permitted to use them,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 4 by showing it depends on one side of a מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The pairing of תרומת הדשן with the יום הכיפורים garments as שני כתובין הבאין כאחד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי דוסא the garments are usable after their מצוה, so they do not share תרומת הדשן's rule. That leaves תרומת הדשן as a lone source that should teach.

steps.title: Pair תרומת הדשן with עגלה ערופה instead
steps.stepSummary: Even for רבי דוסא, תרומת הדשן has a partner, עגלה ערופה. So the two are still שני כתובין הבאין כאחד and teach nothing for other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are two verses that come as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי דוסא by finding a different second source, עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עגלה ערופה stays forbidden for benefit even after its מצוה is done, just like תרומת הדשן. With two sources saying the same thing, the rule of שני כתובין הבאין כאחד blocks learning a general rule from them. This works without depending on the garments at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
Removing a shovelful of ashes from the מזבח each morning
Two verses teaching the same thing, which together do not teach a general rule

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes and the heifer whose neck is broken
are two verses that come as one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by swapping in a new partner source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the garments, תרומת הדשן stands alone for רבי דוסא and should teach a general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: עגלה ערופה shares the same rule, so the two together are שני כתובין הבאין כאחד and do not teach.

steps.title: The answer only works if two verses do not teach
steps.stepSummary: The whole approach works only for the view that שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין. For the view that they do teach, it fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says they do not teach. But according to the one who says they do teach, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a deeper problem with the method it has been using in all the answers so far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת about whether two verses teaching the same thing can teach a general rule. If they can teach, then pairing תרומת הדשן with any partner does not block anything. In that case תרומת הדשן and its partner should together teach that מעילה applies even after an item's מצוה is done.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not teach (a general rule)
They do teach (a general rule)
According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: Every answer so far relied on שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין. Now the גמרא asks what to do for the opinion that they do teach.

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says they do not teach,
phrases.notes: He means two verses that come as one do not teach their shared rule to other cases.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says they do teach,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the shared principle behind the answers in steps 2, 4 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: Relying on the rule that שני כתובין הבאין כאחד do not teach
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that two such verses do teach, the pair should still produce the general rule that מעילה applies even after an item's מצוה is done.

steps.title: Two exclusion words limit the rule to these two cases
steps.stepSummary: Even for the view that שני כתובין הבאין כאחד do teach other cases, here the תורה wrote a limiting word in each case. So only עגלה ערופה and תרומת הדשן have מעילה after their מצוה is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two limiting words are written. There, by the עגלה ערופה, it says 'the one whose neck was broken.' And there, by the ashes, it says 'and he shall put it next to the altar.' These, yes; anything else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7. Each of the two cases has its own limiting word in the פסוק, so nothing else can be learned from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 asked about the view that two similar פסוקים do teach other cases. The answer is that here the תורה went further and wrote an actual מיעוט in each case: 'הערופה' and 'ושמו'. A clear exclusion beats the general rule, so on every view these two cases stand alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Exclusions: words in a פסוק that limit a law to one case only
Two פסוקים that teach the same new law; some say they cannot be used to learn about other cases
These yes, anything else no: the rule applies only here

steps.whatToRemember: Even for the view that שני כתובין הבאין כאחד מלמדין, nothing is learned from עגלה ערופה and תרומת הדשן, because each פסוק has its own exclusion word. So the rule that there is no מעילה after an item's מצוה is done stands on every view.

phrases.english: Two exclusions are written.
It is written there: 'The one whose neck was broken',
phrases.notes: דברים 21:6. The word 'the' points to this one calf only.

phrases.english: and it is written there: 'And he shall put it next to the altar',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:3. 'It' means these ashes, and nothing else.

phrases.english: these, yes,
anything else, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by pointing to explicit exclusion words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a textual exclusion that works on every view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For those who hold שני כתובין הבאין כאחד מלמדין, we could learn from these two cases that other מצוה objects also have מעילה after use.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each פסוק has a מיעוט, so the law is limited to these two cases on every view.

steps.title: Does the משנה about libations disagree with רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: נסכים carry מעילה from the start. It suggests the משנה may not follow רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: libations, at their start, one is liable for מעילה with them, etc. Let us say that our משנה is not like רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It then suggests this משנה might go against a certain תנא; his opinion comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says there is מעילה on נסכים at first, but not once they go down into the drainpipes. The 'לימא' is a suggestion, not a final ruling. The גמרא suspects a conflict with רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק and sets up his ברייתא to show why.

keyTerms.meaning: Libations: wine poured on the מזבח
One is liable for מעילה, using הקדש for personal benefit
'Shall we say...?': a suggestion the גמרא may later reject

phrases.english: Libations, at their outset, one is liable for misusing them, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה, cut off by 'etc.', says that once the wine goes down into the drainpipes, there is no more מעילה.

phrases.english: Let us say that our משנה is not
in accordance with רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק,

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the sugya by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that there is no מעילה on libations once they reach the drainpipes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If another תנא treats the wine in the drainpipes as still holy, the משנה seems to disagree with him.

steps.title: The ברייתא about burning the leftover libation wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק says young כהנים went down into the drainpipes once every seventy years. They took out the hardened wine and burned it בקדושה, learned from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a small opening between the ramp and the מזבח, on the west side of the ramp. Once in seventy years, young כהנים went down into it. They brought up hardened wine that looked like round cakes of pressed figs, and burned it in holiness. As the פסוק says, 'In holiness pour a libation of strong drink to ה׳': just as its pouring is in holiness, so its burning is in holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא behind its suggestion. It shows that the wine in the drainpipes still had to be treated as holy and burned בקדושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine had already gone down into the drainpipes, yet it still needed burning in holiness. That suggests it keeps its קדושה there, which seems to point toward מעילה still applying. That is the opposite of what the משנה says, which is why the גמרא suspected a conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: A small opening or gap
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Young כהנים, not yet fully grown
Wine that hardened and thickened
In holiness, meaning inside the holy area of the עזרה

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says 'מעילה' at all. The question of מעילה comes from the idea that the wine still needs burning in holiness, so it seems to still be holy.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק says:

phrases.aramaic: לוּל קָטָן הָיָה בֵּין כֶּבֶשׁ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: There was a small gap between the ramp and the altar,
on the west side of the ramp.
Once in seventy years
young priests would go down into it,
phrases.notes: They went down to reach the drainpipes under the מזבח, where the poured wine collected.

phrases.english: and bring up congealed wine,
which looked like round cakes of pressed figs,
and they would burn it in holiness.
As it is stated: 'In holiness pour a libation of strong drink to ה׳':
just as its pouring is in holiness,
so too its burning is in holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the suggestion in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that the משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that the leftover libation wine was burned בקדושה, learned from במדבר 28:7

steps.title: Where does the verse teach burning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק quoted in the ברייתא shows that the hardened wine must be burned בקדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses on the ברייתא from Step 10 and asks how its פסוק teaches burning. This sets up רבינא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that the ברייתא quotes speaks about pouring the wine בקודש. It does not mention burning at all. So the גמרא wants to know where the idea of burning comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this shown? Where in the פסוק do we see it?

phrases.english: From where is it inferred?
phrases.notes: He means: the פסוק talks about pouring, so how do we know the hardened wine must be burned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the ruling in the ברייתא quoted in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק cited in the ברייתא shows that the hardened wine must be burned בקדושה.

steps.title: Learning from the word holy by leftover offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבינא links the word קודש by נסכים to the word קודש by נותר. Just as נותר is burned בקדושה, the hardened wine is burned בקדושה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We learn it from the word 'holy' and the word 'holy.' It says here, by נסכים, 'in holiness.' It says there, by leftover offerings, 'You shall burn the leftovers in fire; it may not be eaten, because it is holy.' Just as נותר is burned in holiness, so too this wine is burned in holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question with a גזרה שוה, two places in the תורה that use the same word. The word קודש connects the wine of the נסכים to נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says to burn נותר and calls it קודש. The פסוק about נסכים also uses the word קודש. Because the same word appears in both places, the rule of burning בקדושה carries over from נותר to the hardened wine.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from, meaning it is learned through a link between two פסוקים
Learning a law from the same word used in two places in the תורה
Meat of a קרבן left over past the time it may be eaten, which must be burned
Burning in a holy place and in a holy way

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, according to רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק, the wine is still holy even after it goes down into the pipes. That is exactly why it looks like he disagrees with the משנה.

phrases.english: And Ravina said:
It comes from "holy" and "holy."
It is written here: "In holiness,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:7, said about pouring the wine of the נסכים.

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"You shall burn the leftover in fire
and it shall not be eaten, for they are holy,"
Just as leftover offerings are burned in holiness,
so too, this one is also burned in holiness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by giving the source for burning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה links קודש by נסכים to קודש by נותר, so the hardened wine is burned בקדושה just like נותר.

steps.title: The משנה can follow him, in a case where the wine was caught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on Step 9. The משנה can follow רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק if it is talking about wine that was caught before it reached the bottom of the pipes.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק, in a case where the wine was caught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question from Step 9: does the משנה disagree with רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק? It answers no, because the משנה is talking about a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 suggested that the משנה, which says there is no מעילה once the wine goes down to the pipes, disagrees with רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק. Here the גמרא explains that the משנה means wine that was caught on the way down and never reached the bottom of the pipes. Wine that did reach the bottom becomes holy, and everyone agrees about that wine.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say, meaning the ruling fits even this opinion
It was caught, meaning the wine was collected before reaching the bottom

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק changed his view. It is saying that the משנה is talking about a different case of wine, wine that never reached the bottom of the pipes.

phrases.english: You can even say
it follows Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Tzadok,
where it was caught.
phrases.notes: Some of the wine was caught on the way down and never got to the bottom of the pipes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to Step 9's question and pushes back on the idea that the משנה disagrees with רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion from Step 9 that the משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 9 assumed the משנה was talking about all the wine. Really, it can be talking only about wine that was caught before reaching the bottom of the pipes.

steps.title: Second version: suggesting the משנה follows him
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the discussion turns the same idea into a suggestion: perhaps the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק, in a case where the wine was caught.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: Shall we say that our משנה follows רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק, in a case where the wine was caught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way the discussion was told. In this version, the idea that the משנה matches רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק is raised as a suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the גמרא started with a challenge (the משנה seems to disagree) and then answered it. In this version, the גמרא starts by proposing that the משנה fits רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק only in the case where the wine was caught. That would mean wine that reached the bottom of the pipes is holy and has מעילה. The next step rejects this proposal.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A suggestion that the גמרא is testing

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions differ. In the first, the משנה is about wine that was caught, and wine that reached the bottom of the pipes is holy. In the second, the 'caught' reading is rejected: even wine at the bottom has no holiness מדאורייתא, and burning it is only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Shall we say that our Mishnah
follows Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Tzadok,
where it was caught?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of Steps 9 and 13, where the link between the משנה and רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק is raised as a suggestion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה can be read as following רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק, in the case of wine that was caught before reaching the bottom of the pipes.

steps.title: No, the burning is only a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 14. רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק agrees there is no מעילה on the wine מדאורייתא, and burning it is only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. The burning is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק only in a case where the wine was caught. It gives a different way to fit him with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 suggested we need a special case where the wine was caught before it reached the bottom of the pipes. The גמרא says that is not needed. Even wine that reached the bottom is not holy מדאורייתא, so there is no מעילה, just as the משנה says. רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק's demand to burn it is only a rabbinic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not from the Torah itself
By Torah law. This is the level the גמרא is saying does NOT apply here

steps.confusionAlert: The word לא does not mean רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק disagrees with the משנה. It rejects only the answer in Step 14. The new answer is that he agrees with the משנה מדאורייתא.

phrases.english: They say: No,
phrases.notes: He means: that is not how to fit the משנה with רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק.

phrases.english: and it is by rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: The burning of the hardened wine is only a rabbinic rule. By Torah law, the wine has no מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'wine was caught' suggestion of Step 14 and replaces it with a 'rabbinic only' explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the need to limit the case to wine that was caught before reaching the bottom of the pipes.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes that רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק treats the wine at the bottom of the pipes as holy by Torah law. In fact, his burning rule is only rabbinic.

steps.title: But he quoted a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 15. רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק brought a פסוק for burning the wine, which sounds like a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he quotes a פסוק for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that burning the wine is only a rabbinic rule. It points out that the ברייתא in Step 10 brought a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a sage brings a פסוק as the source for a rule, that normally shows the rule comes from the תורה. That clashes with Step 15, which says the burning is only מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק, a verse
He is taking it, meaning he is quoting it as a source

phrases.english: But he is citing a verse for it?
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק from the ברייתא in Step 10, which רבינא explained through the word קודש in Step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'rabbinic only' answer of Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 15 that burning the wine is only מדרבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Quoting a פסוק as the source implies a Torah-level law, which contradicts a rabbinic-only rule.

steps.title: The פסוק is only a support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is only an אסמכתא, a hint the rabbis attached to their own rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only a supporting hint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in Step 16. The פסוק is not the real source; it is only a support for a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the חכמים make a rule and connect it to a פסוק as a hint or memory aid. That is called an אסמכתא. So quoting the פסוק does not turn the burning into a law מדאורייתא, and Step 15 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק used only as a hint or support for a rabbinic rule, not as its real Torah source

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק fits with the משנה. מדאורייתא there is no מעילה on the wine. Burning it is a rabbinic rule, and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a פסוק quoted for a rule does not always mean the rule comes from the תורה.

phrases.english: It is a mere support.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the פסוק as an אסמכתא rather than a real source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a פסוק was quoted, the burning must be a Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is only a support, so the burning stays a rabbinic rule.

steps.title: New משנה: ashes, the מנורה, and birds of the wrong age
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the ashes of the inner altar and the leftovers of the מנורה may not be used, but there is no מעילה if they are. If someone makes the ashes holy anew, there is מעילה. Birds that are too young or too old follow the same rule as the ashes: no use, but no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ashes removed from the inner altar and from the מנורה: one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה. If someone makes the removed ashes holy from the start, there is מעילה. Turtledoves that are still too young and young pigeons that are already too old: one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists items that may not be used, but whose use does not bring the penalty of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items are still connected to the מקדש, so using them is forbidden. But they are no longer holy in a way that brings the penalty of מעילה. If a person actively makes the ashes holy again, they become fully holy and מעילה applies. The birds of the wrong age cannot be brought as קרבנות, so they also have only the 'no use, no מעילה' status.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing the ashes; here, the ashes that were removed
The inner altar, the golden altar used for קטורת
One may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה if one did
Turtledoves, valid as a קרבן only once they are grown
Young pigeons, valid as a קרבן only while they are young

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not liable for מעילה' does not mean the item is allowed. Using it is still forbidden from the start; only the penalty of מעילה does not apply.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The removed ashes of the inner altar, and of the Candelabrum –
one may not benefit from them, but there is no liability for misuse.
One who consecrates removed ashes anew –
there is liability for misusing it.
Turtledoves whose time has not arrived,
phrases.notes: They are still too young to be brought as a קרבן.

phrases.english: and young pigeons whose time has passed –
phrases.notes: They are already too old to be brought as a קרבן.

phrases.english: one may not benefit from them, but there is no liability for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removed ashes of the inner altar and of the מנורה, and birds of the wrong age for a קרבן, may not be used, but there is no מעילה. Ashes that are made holy anew do bring מעילה.

steps.title: The גמרא opens its question on the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a question with the word בשלמא, 'granted', about the משנה's rule for the inner altar's ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its first question on the new משנה. The full question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בשלמא means 'it makes sense for one case.' The question that follows will ask why a different case is not the same. Here we see only the opening word, so the content of the question comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted', 'it makes sense'; it opens a question that compares one case to another

phrases.english: GEMARA: Granted

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A question about the משנה's rule, starting from what makes sense in one case. The details continue in the next part of the text.
